Part of [AGENTIC-2895](https://linear.app/agenticassets/issue/AGENTIC-2895).

`buildout_observation_manifest.py` is a standalone, default-off **offline integrity experiment**. It has no network, database client, scheduler, ingestion integration, production writer, DDL, or permission grant. Input, artifact, and manifest are unreviewed private data; do not commit, upload, share, or feed them to ingestion. The underlying artifact's heuristic quarantine is not a confidentiality guarantee.

`seal` takes the original saved input and the corresponding artifact, independently computes their byte hashes, rebuilds the artifact with the current local builder and requires byte-for-byte equality. It records the builder artifact schema and SHA-256 of the local builder module and current source-key registry, source, generation, capture, page, transaction (`sale`, `lease`, or `unknown`), input kind, and builder summary including quarantine and upstream omission counts. The source and all scope fields are **operator assertions**, not evidence that the source owns the content, that the capture is current or complete, or that storage and use are authorized. `verify` requires the caller to supply an expected scope independently, rehashes both supplied files and rebuilds the artifact again. Mismatches fail closed.

The manifest digest detects accidental or uncoordinated changes; it is **not a digital signature or authentication**. A caller who controls the files and asserted scope can recompute it. The builder fingerprint identifies the locally readable file, not a verified Git tree or trusted executable; parent directories, interpreter, local filesystem and inputs are not sandboxed or authenticated. A separate reviewed source-rights decision, owned collection proof, signed or otherwise trusted manifest binding, retention policy and security admission remain necessary before any live writer. The original source input remains necessary for byte-exact recovery, quarantined content and numeric spelling; the manifest does not contain source evidence values.

The process-local `FixtureReplayModel` accepts only input labelled `syntheticFixture`, preserves record content in memory, and models atomic retry/conflict handling for independently verified manifests. That label is caller-controlled, not a security boundary. A page slot includes asserted source, generation, page, and transaction, so page ordinals do not collide. A second invariant binds the asserted source, generation and page to one input hash, artifact hash, capture ID, builder and summary across all transaction labels. Different transaction-page payloads require distinct asserted page identifiers. Capture ID is bound metadata, not a separate slot: changing it for the same page is a divergent replay. These identifiers remain unverified caller assertions. Exact retries are unchanged; different sealed content or metadata in a slot is refused. A different generation is a separate capture, not proof of a real new listing or authoritative chronology. Nothing is written to canonical listings, children, lifecycle, source index, receipts, or an external system. The model is not a durable writer or database concurrency proof.

Outputs are exclusively created with mode 0600 and cannot overwrite an existing destination or follow a final symlink. Caller-controlled parent paths remain outside this guarantee. From a standalone `git clone --no-hardlinks`, run `python3 -m pytest tests/test_buildout_observation_manifest.py tests/test_buildout_observation_artifact.py -q`. Use `python3 buildout_observation_manifest.py --help` for file-only `seal` and `verify` arguments. Keep all resulting files in private ignored scratch storage and review source rights independently before any later use.

Each original, artifact, manifest and locally fingerprinted module file is read through its own bounded, final-symlink-rejecting descriptor with pre/post change detection. These are per-file checks, not an atomic multi-file snapshot or source authentication; parent directories, metadata-concealing filesystems and changes after return are outside the guarantee. Native Windows lacks the required no-follow behavior and fails closed; use WSL. This release adds the reader module fingerprint. Current verification deliberately rejects earlier seals. Retain the original input, artifact and old manifest. If the current builder reproduces the old artifact byte-for-byte, create and verify a new manifest at a new private path. If it does not, use the matching prior code to verify the old seal, or build a new artifact and manifest at new private paths; never assume a changed builder can reseal old bytes. Never delete prior evidence merely to regenerate a seal.
